title: world-heavyweight-championship-iga-2003
label: "The Expert" Matt Allen

won.source: The promotion's served card of The Battle for Fort Knox, 26 August 2001.

lost.source: Lost to Todd Bishop in a scaffold match at Requiem for Pain, 31 October 2001.

how: Won the round robin decider against Mark Davenport to become the first IGA World Heavyweight Champion.
note: The first champion of the title.

title: world-heavyweight-championship-iga-2003
label: Todd Bishop

won.source: The promotion's served card of Requiem for Pain, 31 October 2001.

lost.source: Lost to the debuting Nightstalker on the served card of Combat Zone, 2 January 2002, in what the referee ruled after the fact a triangle match; Jazz Madison assisted at ringside.

how: Won a scaffold match against Matt Allen.
note: Defended against Scott Sexton, Luther Harden, the Dirty Dog Posse, Carl Blair and Tommy Danger in the served 2001 cards, and again against Scott Sexton in a Japanese Death Match on the served card of 2 January 2002 before losing the title later the same night.

title: tv-championship-iga-2003
label: Maxime St. Jean

won.source: The promotion's served card of The Battle for Fort Knox, 26 August 2001.

lost.source: Lost to Sparrow Jinn on the promotion's served card of 4 July 2002. The 18 June 2002 card billed Todd Bishop as the current TV Champion instead, a claim every other served card contradicts, including this 4 July card itself, which calls Maxime "the undefeatable former TV Champion" on his loss here; the Bishop billing is recorded separately as a flagged, likely-erroneous one-off (see this title's reigns-append note).

how: Won a six-man elimination match.
note: The first champion of the title; defended against Mark Davenport, Malik Johnson and Dan Watterson in the served cards.

title: jr-heavyweight-championship-iga-2003
label: "Defiant" Ryan Arnott

won.source: The tournament final against Nick Hart was set on the served card of 26 September 2001, and Arnott was champion by the served card of 18 October 2001; the final itself is not among the served cards.

lost.source: Lost to Lazz Sterling on the served card of 9 January 2002, after Maxime St. Jean struck him with the TV title belt.

how: Won the tournament for the vacant title.
note: The first champion of the title; retained in a five-man ladder match at Devil's Night and against El Rico, Kerry Treadwell, Lazz Sterling and Lenny.

title: world-tag-team-championship-iga-2003
label: Forever Unchained

won.source: Forever Unchained were set to meet Estrago and Malik Johnson for the first championship on the served card of 26 September 2001 and were champions by the served card of 18 October 2001; the final is not among the served cards.

lost.source: Lost on the served card of 9 January 2002; Pandemonium was absent from the match, defended in his place by Phantom Stranger alongside Mark Davenport.

how: Won the tag team tournament final.
note: The first champions of the title; retained in a triangle match, in a steel cage at Requiem for Pain, and against Carl Blair and Jarred Bombay. Lost on 9 January 2002 with Phantom Stranger standing in for Pandemonium.

title: fight-club-championship-iga-2003
label: Malkav

won.source: The promotion's served card of Devil's Night, 30 October 2001.

lost.source: Still champion after a locker-room defence against Gehenna at the Tournament of Warriors, 23 December 2001.

how: Won a three-way match with Greg Vaughn and Eric Henry at the Last Chance Bar & Grille.
note: The first holder of the title the served cards record. Gehenna was champion by 3 April 2002; no surviving document shows the change from Malkav.

title: euro-championship-iga-2003
label: Estrago

won.source: The promotion's served card of 7 November 2001.

lost.source: Lost to the debuting Anatole Lee on the served card of 14 March 2002 (The End).

how: Won a ten-man elimination match.
note: The first champion of the title; defended against Nick Hart, Marco Avery, and (by count-out, retaining) Big Smoothie on 7 March 2002.

title: international-championship-iga-2003
label: Mark Davenport

won.source: The promotion's served card of Combat Zone, 2 January 2002.

lost.source: Lost to Pandemonium on the served card of International Incident, 24 February 2002, in a special stipulations match after "Mr. Magnificent" Mikel ambushed both competitors and the referee.

how: Won a battle royal for the vacant title's number-one contendership, then beat Donovan Keltrane after a rival promotion's Jeff Keenan interfered.
note: The first IGA International Champion.

title: world-heavyweight-championship-iga-2003
label: The Nightstalker

won.source: The promotion's served card of Combat Zone, 2 January 2002.

lost.source: Lost to Todd Bishop on the served card of 23 January 2002, an Iron Man Japanese Death Match, 7 falls to 5.

how: Interfered on his debut against a battered Todd Bishop immediately after Bishop's Japanese Death Match defence against Scott Sexton, pinning him with Jazz Madison at ringside in what the referee ruled a triangle match.
note: Retained on the served card of 9 January 2002 (a steel cage escape, with Jazz Madison's help against Matt Allen).

title: jr-heavyweight-championship-iga-2003
label: Lazz Sterling

won.source: The promotion's served card of 9 January 2002.

lost.source: Not documented among the served cards; Ash was champion by 16 May 2002.

how: Beat champion Ryan Arnott after Maxime St. Jean struck Arnott with the TV title belt.
note: Sterling's own tenure widened with a note about winning a rival promotion's own interfed title on 20 March 2002.

title: world-tag-team-championship-iga-2003
label: Rage and Donovan Keltrane

won.source: The promotion's served card of 9 January 2002.

lost.source: Lost on the served card of 2 May 2002, when Rage turned on his own partner, Donovan Keltrane, chokeslamming him.

how: Beat a stand-in Forever Unchained lineup (Mark Davenport and Phantom Stranger, filling in for Pandemonium) with the Dark Messenger, a top-rope cross backbreaker into a gutbuster stunner.
note: Billed under no team name of their own in the served text.

title: world-heavyweight-championship-iga-2003
label: Todd Bishop

won.source: The promotion's served card of 23 January 2002.

lost.source: Lost to Sean Smith on the served card of International Incident, 24 February 2002, a Born to Be Wired match, by submission to the Seanshooter.

how: Won an Iron Man Japanese Death Match 7 falls to 5, the last through three panes of glass and a bed of nails; Matt Allen, betrayed by Jazz Madison mid-match, turned on the Dynasty and helped him.

title: international-championship-iga-2003
label: Pandemonium

won.source: The promotion's served card of International Incident, 24 February 2002.

lost.source: Vacated on the promotion's served card of 30 May 2002.

how: Beat champion Mark Davenport, his own Forever Unchained partner, in a special stipulations match after "Mr. Magnificent" Mikel ambushed both men and the special guest referee, Phantom Stranger, then drove off with Davenport locked in an ambulance.
note: Vacated by Jazz Madison's own announcement, citing an unshown injury ("crashed and burned"); the promotion announced a Team Challenge Series with a Battle Royal to crown a new champion, rather than giving the title outright to number-one contender Scottie Page.

title: world-heavyweight-championship-iga-2003
label: Sean Smith

won.source: The promotion's served card of International Incident, 24 February 2002.

lost.source: Lost to Mark Davenport on the promotion's served card of 23 June 2002 (Team Challenge Series / Pandemonium).

how: Beat champion Todd Bishop in the main event, a Born to Be Wired match, submitting him to the Seanshooter after Delilah pulled Candi Caine off the apron.
note: Retained against Tommy Danger at the pay-per-view GrappleFest, 21 April 2002 (not among the served documents; recorded from the promotion's own recap on the served card of 2 May 2002). Retained against Sebastian Manning on 23 May 2002 by pinning him with the title belt after Mark Davenport's interference nearly cost Smith the match.

title: euro-championship-iga-2003
label: Anatole Lee

won.source: The promotion's served card of 14 March 2002.

lost.source: Lost to Donovan Keltrane on the promotion's served card of 23 May 2002.

how: Beat champion Estrago on his in-ring debut with The End, a front-facelock reverse DDT.
note: Lost the title in a steel cage escape match; AsH, uninvolved in the match, threw weapons into the cage and then pulled Lee off the top of the cage in a suicide dive, costing him the race to the floor.

title: fight-club-championship-iga-2003
label: Malik Johnson

won.source: The promotion's served card of 3 April 2002.

lost.source: Not documented among the served cards; Big Smoothie was champion by 16 May 2002.

how: Beat champion Gehenna at a convenience store, with Cole Thorne's help (a baseball bat and a cash register).

title: fight-club-championship-iga-2003
label: Rage

won.source: The promotion's served card of 23 May 2002.

lost.source: Not documented among the served cards; Big Smoothy was champion again by 30 October 2002, called "self proclaimed Fight Club Icon" and defending the title on that card.

how: Hardcore triple threat; locked challenger Big Smoothie (the champion) inside a locker room, then pinned the other challenger, "Tacks" Paul Barker. (ended: unknown)

title: world-tag-team-championship-iga-2003
label: Maxime St. Jean and Anatole Lee

won.source: The promotion's served card of 2 May 2002.

lost.source: Lost to the Chosen Ones on the promotion's served card of 30 May 2002.

how: Beat champions Rage and Donovan Keltrane after Rage turned on his own partner mid-match, chokeslamming him for the pin.
note: Lost the titles to the Chosen Ones (Buddy Drifter and Apocalypse) while Lee was not the legal man, a finish AsH's distraction was a factor in.

title: jr-heavyweight-championship-iga-2003
label: Sebastian Manning

won.source: The promotion's served card of 11 July 2002.

lost.source: Not documented among the served cards; Cyril Lesley held the title by 31 October 2002 (Requiem for Pain).

how: Won a battle royal (also featuring Scott Sexton, Nick Hart, Michael McCarey, Lenny, the outgoing champion Estrago, Cyril Lesley, Adam Ross, Ryan Arnott and T-Sizzle) by throwing T-Sizzle over the top rope last. (ended: unknown)
note: Attacked with a chair and had the title held up by "Vile Vince Viper" immediately after the match, as though Viper had won it; no title change resulted.

title: fight-club-championship-iga-2003
label: Ryan Williams

won.source: The promotion's served card of 30 October 2002 (Devil's Night 2), a Haunted House match against Big Smoothy.

lost.source: Still champion on the served card of 30 October 2002; no later change is among the served cards.

how: Big Smoothy was piledriven through a table by a man costumed as Pennywise the Clown, whose identity and reason for helping Williams are not shown; Williams made the cover.
note: The identity of the man in the Pennywise costume is not revealed among the served cards.

title: womens-championship-iga-2003
label: Myranda "The Cat" Steele

won.source: Not documented among the served cards; champion by 16 May 2002.

lost.source: Not documented among the served cards; commentary on the served card of 1 September 2002 places the loss to Lara Leigh Love "back in July".

how: (ended: unknown)
note: The first champion the served cards record.

title: euro-championship-iga-2003
label: "Darkheart" Donovan Keltrane

won.source: The promotion's served card of 23 May 2002.

lost.source: Not documented among the served cards; the title was vacant by 8 August 2002, when a tournament crowned a new champion.

how: Steel cage escape match; won the race to the floor after AsH (uninvolved in the match) pulled champion Anatole Lee off the top of the cage.

title: fight-club-championship-iga-2003
label: Gehenna

won.source: Not documented among the served cards; champion by 3 April 2002.

lost.source: Lost to Malik Johnson on the served card of 3 April 2002.

note: Won the title from Malkav at some point not among the served cards.

title: world-tag-team-championship-iga-2003
label: The Chosen Ones

won.source: The promotion's served card of 30 May 2002.

lost.source: Not documented among the served cards; the Deadly Alliance (Tommy Danger and Todd Bishop) held the titles by 18 June 2002.

how: Apocalypse pinned Anatole Lee (not the legal man) after a chokeslam, with AsH's ringside distraction a factor.

title: jr-heavyweight-championship-iga-2003
label: Ash

won.source: Not documented among the served cards; champion by 16 May 2002.

lost.source: Not documented among the served cards; Estrago said in his own promo of 6 June 2002 that he had already won the title "but not the way I wanted", champion by then.

note: Billed "Undisputed Junior Heavyweight Champion of the World", the interfed title Lazz Sterling won on 20 March 2002, since unified with the IGA's own Jr. Heavyweight Championship. Retained against Cyril Lesley on 23 May 2002.

title: world-tag-team-championship-iga-2003
label: The Chosen Ones (Drifter and Powers)

won.source: The promotion's served card of 18 June 2002 (1 of 7 parts held).

lost.source: Lost to the Deadly Alliance (Tommy Danger and Todd Bishop) on the promotion's served card of 11 July 2002, a steel cage match.

how: Won the rematch after Xander Xaviero (Jazz Madison's enforcer) interfered, powerslamming Tommy Danger for the pin.
note: Drifter's partner began billing himself "Marc Powers" as of this show; confirmed the same performer as Apocalypse by the 11 July 2002 card's own text (see apoc-iga-2003).

title: world-tag-team-championship-iga-2003
label: The Deadly Alliance (Danger and Bishop)

won.source: The promotion's served card of 11 July 2002, a steel cage match; the challengers won clean.

lost.source: Not documented among the served cards; the Chosen Ones (Drifter and Powers) held the titles again by 25 July 2002, called "the tag team champion[s]" on that card's own text.

how: Steel cage, pin-or-submit-only; Bishop threw Danger off the top of the cage onto Powers for the pin, then moonsaulted off the cage himself onto Drifter for good measure (not needed for the actual fall). (ended: unknown)
note: The label 'The Deadly Alliance' was used once before, for an earlier, undocumented and separately flagged claim to the titles; this reign is the fully documented one.

title: tv-championship-iga-2003
label: Sparrow Jinn

won.source: The promotion's served card of 4 July 2002.

lost.source: Not documented among the served cards; Todd Bishop held the title by 24 October 2002, seen defending it there in commentary.

how: Submission (a modified Dragon Sleeper) in the show's main event. (ended: unknown)

title: world-heavyweight-championship-iga-2003
label: "The Eternal Rebel" Mark Davenport

won.source: The promotion's served card of 23 June 2002 (Team Challenge Series / Pandemonium), billed as the 5th champion in company history.

lost.source: Lost to Scottie Page on the promotion's served card of 15 August 2002.

how: No-DQ match; won with a piledriver off a high vertical suplex after Smith missed a Shooting Sean Press through a table.
note: Retained on the served card of 1 August 2002, a Four Way Dance also involving Buddy Drifter, "Marc Powers" (Apocalypse) and Sebastian Manning, pinning Drifter after Powers and Manning were eliminated. Attacked immediately after the 23 June 2002 match by the Nightstalker, who took the title belt and dropped it across Davenport's face before leaving; no title change resulted.

title: international-championship-iga-2003
label: "High Risk" Lazz Sterling

won.source: The promotion's served card of 23 June 2002 (Team Challenge Series / Pandemonium).

lost.source: Still champion on the served card of 23 June 2002; no later change is among the served cards.

how: Won an 11-man battle royal for the vacant title (Tommy Danger, Donovan Keltrane, Devante Anderson, Ryan Arnott, T-Sizzle, Buddy Drifter, Cyril Lesley, Michael McCarey, Anatole Lee and AsH also entered) after Jazz Madison's enforcer Xander Xaviero interfered against the last other man, Tommy Danger.
note: The recovering former champion, Pandemonium, returned on crutches after the match, handed the title over on request, then attacked Sterling with a crutch and vowed to reclaim it. Retained on 24 October 2002 against Mark Davenport (Buddy Drifter's interference turned the tables); Lenny earned a shot by winning a mini-tournament over Michael McCarey and Vile Vince Viper on 30 October 2002 (Devil's Night 2); Sterling then retained against Lenny in a steel cage on 31 October 2002 (Requiem for Pain), escaping through the door.

title: tv-championship-iga-2003
label: "Simply Sadistic" Damian Payne

won.source: The promotion's served card of 31 October 2002 (Requiem for Pain), a Tuxedo match against Jackson Phillips for the vacated title.

lost.source: Not documented among the served cards; Jackson Phillips regained the title in an undocumented rematch "two weeks" after Requiem for Pain, per Damian Payne's own promo on the 1 December 2002 card.

how: Stripped Phillips' tuxedo pants off after a Chokebomb to the floor. (ended: unknown)
note: Billed as the IGA's third TV champion in 14 months.

title: world-tag-team-championship-iga-2003
label: Breaking and Entering

won.source: The promotion's served card of 1 September 2002 (Chance Encounters), a Boston Street Fight.

lost.source: Lost to the Pimps of the Nation on the promotion's served card of 31 October 2002 (Requiem for Pain), a Sledgehammer/Ladders/Chairs match.

how: Kenny Denmark pinned Buddy Drifter after a top-rope DDT off a steel scaffold, with Quentin Avery adding a second man to the pin; Xavier Springer (returning from injury) and manager Rachel Skye both factored into the finish.
note: Retained on 24 October 2002 against Tommy Danger and Corey Irons, a match interrupted before the bell by Scottie Page and David Hagen, with Lazz Sterling's mid-match chair shots also a factor; Denmark pinned Irons with his own feet illegally on the ropes.

won.source: Not documented among the served cards; champion by 6 June 2002, by Estrago's own account not in the way he wanted.

lost.source: Eliminated in a battle royal for the title on the promotion's served card of 11 July 2002; the card does not otherwise document any defense between 6 June and this loss.

title: euro-championship-iga-2003
label: Byron B. Buffington

won.source: The promotion's served card of 8 August 2002.

lost.source: Not documented among the served cards; Speedy Irons held the title by 1 December 2002.

how: Won a tournament for the vacant title; in the 3-way final (also featuring Victor Vegas and Devante Anderson), Christopher Scarlet interfered against Anderson's own backup, Corey Irons, at ringside, and Buffington pinned Anderson using a shoe smuggled in by manager Jason LaPlante. (ended: unknown)
note: The tournament bracket is not fully documented: Victor Vegas entered at what the card calls "Round 2" with no 1st-round match shown (an apparent bye), and 1st-round winners Estrago and Devante Anderson each advance with no shown semifinal -- flagged, not filled in.

title: world-heavyweight-championship-iga-2003
label: "Sensational" Scottie Page

won.source: The promotion's served card of 15 August 2002.

lost.source: Vacated on the promotion's served card of 31 October 2002 (Requiem for Pain); Page was not medically cleared after the injuries sustained at Devil's Night 2 the night before.

how: Referee Erik Rockwell was knocked out mid-match; Page then struck Davenport with a chair, hit "That's Sensational!", and pinned him once Rockwell recovered.
note: Substituted in after AsH, the originally scheduled challenger, was found beaten and driven through a rental car's windshield earlier on the same card; Todd Bishop and the absent Adam Ross were both suspected on-air. Referee Erik Rockwell was knocked out mid-match; Page struck Davenport with a chair to finish him, then a closing video, framed as amateur camcorder footage, revealed Page himself had carried out the earlier attack on AsH. Retained on 1 September 2002 (Chance Encounters) against a randomly-drawn Damian Payne, a chaos match with interference from Lazz Sterling, Tommy Danger, Mark Davenport and AsH; won with a chair-assisted super shoulder breaker.

title: world-tag-team-championship-iga-2003
label: The Pimps of the Nation

won.source: The promotion's served card of 31 October 2002 (Requiem for Pain), a Sledgehammer/Ladders/Chairs match.

lost.source: Still champions on the served card of 31 October 2002; no later change is among the served cards.

how: Pimp Daddy planted Quentin Avery face-first onto a sledgehammer with the Hizoe Down for the pin.

title: world-tag-team-championship-iga-2003
label: The Deadly Alliance

won.source: Not documented among the served cards; champions by 18 June 2002. Their own broadcast calls this reign shorter than a still-running Fight Club match.

lost.source: Lost to the Chosen Ones on the promotion's served card of 18 June 2002 (1 of 7 parts held).

how: Lost a rematch to the Chosen Ones (now Buddy Drifter and Marc Powers, replacing Apocalypse) after Xander Xaviero interfered, powerslamming Danger for the pin.
note: A mysterious "Beast" speared Bishop mid-match; his allegiance is unclear on the surviving text.

title: womens-championship-iga-2003
label: "Bad Attitude" Lara Leigh Love

won.source: Not documented among the served cards; commentary on the served card of 1 September 2002 places the win over Myranda Steele "back in July".

lost.source: Still champion on the served card of 1 September 2002, retaining a six-way "first pinfall wins" defence; no later change is among the served cards.

how: Not documented among the served cards.
note: Retained on 1 September 2002 (Chance Encounters) in a six-pack challenge against Tawny Blake, London Matthews, Sarah Mayson, Iris Galiver and Jasolyn Brians, pinning Blake after cousin Andy Madison's crutch shot; immediately turned on Blake post-match despite their family tie. Retained again on 31 October 2002 (Requiem for Pain) against Iris Galiver, with guest referee Tawny Blake (Love's cousin) making the final count; Love then attacked Blake post-match anyway.

title: fight-club-championship-iga-2003
label: Big Smoothie

won.source: Not documented among the served cards; champion by 16 May 2002.

lost.source: Lost to Rage on the promotion's served card of 23 May 2002.

note: Lost the title in a hardcore triple threat with Rage and "Tacks" Paul Barker; Rage locked Smoothie inside a locker room and pinned Barker for the title.

title: fight-club-championship-iga-2003
label: Big Smoothy

won.source: Not documented among the served cards; champion again by the served card of 30 October 2002.

lost.source: Lost to Ryan Williams on the promotion's served card of 30 October 2002 (Devil's Night 2), a Haunted House match.

how: Piledriven through a table by an unidentified man costumed as Pennywise the Clown, who then left; Williams pinned him.

title: tv-championship-iga-2003
label: Todd Bishop

won.source: Not documented among the served cards; champion by 18 June 2002.

lost.source: One-off billing, not corroborated by any other served card; see note.

note: FLAGGED, LIKELY ERRONEOUS: the 18 June 2002 card is the only served document billing Bishop as champion. Every other served card, including the 4 July 2002 card that has Maxime St. Jean lose the title to Sparrow Jinn there, treats Maxime as reigning champion throughout without interruption. Recorded as billed on 18 June, but this reign is not treated as real for the purpose of the title's own lineage.

title: tv-championship-iga-2003
label: Todd Bishop (2nd reign)

won.source: Not documented among the served cards; champion again by 24 October 2002.

lost.source: Stripped by Jazz Madison on the promotion's served card of 31 October 2002 (Requiem for Pain) after refusing to defend the title in a Tuxedo match against Jackson Phillips.

note: Refused the wheel-picked Tuxedo match stipulation on principle, attacked Madison and Phillips with his cane, and destroyed the wheel itself.

title: jr-heavyweight-championship-iga-2003
label: Cyril Lesley

won.source: Not documented among the served cards; champion by 31 October 2002.

lost.source: Still champion on the served card of 31 October 2002 (Requiem for Pain), retaining a 7-man ladder match; no later change is among the served cards.

how: Grabbed the belt off a swaying ladder as it toppled, letting himself fall with it to keep from being knocked off first.
note: Defended against Estrago, Ryan Arnott, Vic Parker, Manson, Aaron Stile and Hallowe'en Jack; Manson was stretchered out after a Tombstone Piledriver off a ladder through a table.

title: world-tag-team-championship-iga-2003
label: The Chosen Ones (2nd reign)

won.source: Not documented among the served cards; champions again by the served card of 25 July 2002 (one part of the 18 July 2002 card, part 6, was not served).

lost.source: Lost to Breaking and Entering on the promotion's served card of 1 September 2002 (Chance Encounters), a Boston Street Fight.

how: Not documented among the served cards.
note: Confirmed as champions on the served card of 1 August 2002 and 8 August 2002 as well.

title: world-heavyweight-championship-iga-2003
label: Tommy Danger

won.source: The promotion's served card of 31 October 2002 (Requiem for Pain), a falls-count-anywhere match (starting in the Staples Center's boiler room) against Corey Irons for the vacated title.

lost.source: Still champion on the served card of 31 October 2002; no later change is among the served cards.

how: A high-flying cross body in the ring for the pin, after a marathon match that opened with Danger disguised as Irons for a mind-games angle in the boiler room; "Erik Rockwell", the match's second referee, was revealed mid-match as a disguised Pandemonium interfering against Danger before being chased off.
note: Wheelchair-bound Dirk O'Malley, Danger's retired mentor, stood from his chair at ringside to urge Danger up off the mat late in the match. Retained on 1 December 2002 against Mark Davenport by disqualification, after a returning Patrick McGrath ("The Emerald City Kidd") interfered for Davenport.

title: euro-championship-iga-2003
label: Speedy Irons

won.source: Not documented among the served cards; champion by 1 December 2002.

lost.source: Not documented among the served cards; referenced only in Irons' own on-air breakdown on the promotion's served card of 1 December 2002, which does not give a date for the loss.

note: Irons suffered an on-air breakdown after the loss, repeatedly insisting it was "a bad dream" and demanding Rowlands return to "finish" a match Irons insisted hadn't happened; taken out by stretcher.

title: euro-championship-iga-2003
label: Tommy Rowlands

won.source: Not documented among the served cards; referenced only in Speedy Irons' own on-air breakdown on the promotion's served card of 1 December 2002, which does not give a date for the loss.

lost.source: Still champion on the served card of 1 December 2002; no later change is among the served cards.

note: The title win itself is not documented among the served cards; Rowlands is not shown carrying the belt on this card.

title: tv-championship-iga-2003
label: Jackson Phillips (2nd reign)

won.source: Not documented among the served cards; per Damian Payne's own promo on 1 December 2002, Phillips beat Payne for the title in a rematch "two weeks" after Requiem for Pain, with help from Matt Allen.

lost.source: Still champion on the served card of 1 December 2002; no later change is among the served cards.

note: Not defended on this card; Phillips instead wrestled a non-title Tournament of Warriors qualifier, losing to the Nightstalker.
